questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That is was another culture with a wide option of subjects.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Italy is a beautiful country, and the ESN was really good at making us feel at home! However the University lacked organising skills. The classrooms assigned were too small, it took them too long to give the class another room, some of the teachers did not follow the exam dates (chose other dates) etc. At one campus sight where we spend an entire day every week, there were not wi-fi and no heat.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was hard. The University really did have anything figured out before we started. There were much more classes than stated on the website. They kind of took it as it came, which was difficult for an Erasmus student to do.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The ESN helped with the social aspects. When it came to the class, we just had to figure it out on our own and help each other.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The social aspect was amazing, but not the University itself.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Looked for campus housing but everything was very fast filled.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Start in good time. It is expensive living in Milan, and if you want to live in Campus housing you should apply in good time. If you want to live off campus, also look in good time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was not possible to register before two days before start. And this they told ud about a week before start. So it was impossible to plan anything.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I did not really register. We just sent our Erasmus application through the platform and then an email with our name, number, address etc. and then we were giving a university card and an access to the mail and uni platform.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help through mail. But not a lot.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful but the process was a little forced because it only was possible to register a few days before start.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not panic when you cannot register in good time. They just do everything last minute.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some of the classes seemed at a lower level than anticipated. And one class was only 6 ECTS but the workload was much more. It really depended on which class it was.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was all MA sources, but the level felt BA comparing to my home university.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were no books everything was online which was nice. There was not as much group work as there is in UCPH which I thought was nice. Otherwise pretty much the same.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: European Labour Law, Sustainable Transport, Comparative Contract Law, An Introduction to Italian Private Law in a comparative perspective, Law and Philosophy in a cross-cultural perspective

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Sustainable Transport was an amazing course. The teacher was really nice and his English was good. The exam was two papers through the semester which was a nice way of doing an exam. It was intersting and like nothing I learned at home. 

The other courses was nice as well, except European Labour Law. The workload was way to much, the teacher was not always that nice, had no structure and kept getting off topic.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Some extra things to the apartment. Otherwise I had budget for the rest.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food in the supermarked was either way less or more. Meat is more expensive the rest is cheaper. Going out to eat can be really cheap also drinks. Night clubs are really expensive. Public transportation is cheap also getting an italian number so you have free acces to data was cheap. Traviling by train/bus to other cities is also cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not hear anything about social activities in the University, but perhaps because of covid.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: ESN help you meet other people - but it is outside the University

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: ESN help you meet other people and do something - but it is outside the University

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel to other cities. The bus/train tickets can be cheap so it is a good possibility.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy with the people and culture in that way, but I did not adjust to how the University and teachers did not plan ahead. It was often a big chaos.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to ESN activities - in that way I socialized with a lot of people. Everyone is really nice, so do not be afraid to ask people to hang out. 10/10 they say yes. If you are more people from the same country then try to talk to some people from other countries.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That Italians do not plan, think ahead or inform. That is very frustrating. Like one week before your exam, you don't know how the exam will be or your landlord removing the washer while you are away without informing of this.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That people are out a lot. Restaurants, bars and streets are always filled and there is a nice atmosphere because of this. I felt very safe in Milan even if it is a big city

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Search for a place to live in a good time. 
2. Try not to panic when they don't inform you about anything. Ask and wait. They just do it in another paste.
3. Enjoy it! The time goes by so fast. Even though it is school the academic level is not as high so you will have more free time to enjoy your time in Italy.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Get an Italian phone number. It is like 75kr a month and then you have free access to the data. 
Travel to other cities. You will not regret it.
Involve yourself in the ESN. I did go to a lot of events in the beginning and found a lot of friends this way.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in another country and figuring out things on my own, getting to know a lot of really nice people and seeing many parts of Italy.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing home and trying to figure out what to do, when the Italians did not provide the information as needed.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Some people speak English but others not a lot. Knowing a bit of Italian helped me. I used Duolingo. There is also an Italian Course. I did not attend but heard from others that it was not that helpfull.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
